nodes.question: Is the mug positioned to the right of the headphones?

nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, what evidence indicates whether the source mug moved toward the right of the headphones, and whether a mug at the target is instead additional while the source mug remains elsewhere?

Fail only if clear evidence shows no movement toward that position and the right-side mug is distinct or otherwise unrelated. Unknown if correspondence or movement cannot be determined; do not infer movement or its absence from a right-side mug alone.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

findings.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
findings.question: Does the edited image show the original blue mug moved to the right of the headphones, or does it show a different mug there while the original remains elsewhere?
findings.criteria: Compare the source mug’s distinctive appearance and position with the edited image. Distinguish evidence of the original mug’s relocation from mere presence of any mug on the right; if correspondence is unclear, report unknown rather than treating it as proof either way.
findings.evidence: The source shows one large light-blue mug left of the headphones. The edited image shows a blue blurred patch at the former left location, a small mug near the headphones, and another mug to their right. The right-side mug appears different from the source mug, but the patch and other mug do not conclusively establish what happened to the original.
findings.rationale: The existing s3 observations disagree on whether there is evidence of movement, while the fulfillment readout treats the right-side mug alone as sufficient for completion. A focused comparison is needed to avoid both overclaiming completion from an additional mug and underclaiming if the original mug was moved.
